note: Exploration lists (Madduru near Amaravati, Guntur; Nelakondapalli stupa); no Xiyu ji location.

author: Ajit Kumar Prasad, Directorate of Archaeology, Government of Bihar
asr_identification: Taradih mound at Bodh Gaya (Gaya); Pala monastic complex
evidence: 1987-88: seven periods from neolithic to Pala; Period VI Gupta brick structures, votive stupas, Buddha images, seals; Period VII Pala monastery-complex with terracotta seals and sealings, votive stupas
quote: resumed excavation at Taradhi mound under the general supervision of Prakash Charan Prasad. The main objectives of this year's operation were to spot out the brick built monastic complex of the Pala period … Period VII was distinguished by antiquities of the Pala period and remains of a monastery-complex, terracotta seals and sealings, votive stupas, chhatravalis, etc.
note: The report does not name Xuanzang or the Mahabodhi sangharama. Taradih is the mound N of the Mahabodhi temple (see 492), i.e. Mizutani's 'great monastery' mound (08.06.30); the Gupta and Pala monastic remains fit his identification but no seal naming the monastery is reported.

author: B. M. Pande, Institute of Archaeology, Archaeological Survey of India
evidence: 1987-88: mound 900 x 500 m, 15-23 m high; sequence Kushana to Mughal (some PGW-lineage sherds); Pushyabhuti/Vardhana period massive brick building (wall of 99+ courses), stone inscription fragment in 7th-c. characters; defence wall from post-Gupta times
quote: The mound which is also called locally as the Harsh-ka-Tila measures about 900 x 500 metres and is between 15 and 23 metres in height … The Pushyabhuti or Vardhana period (middle of the sixth to end of seventh century) was distinguished by a massive brick building and other structural remains
note: Thanesar = Sthanesvara taken for granted (Mizutani 04.08; asr: Cunningham, Thanesar fort and town). First excavation of the mound: the Vardhana (Harsha's dynasty) occupation of Xuanzang's time is attested; no Buddhist remains (Xuanzang's stupa N/NW of the city, Cunningham's Madrasa mound, not touched).
Exploration list (Kashipura, East Nimar: microliths, medieval mound); OCR false match for Kashipur.
Balikeshwara temple excavation (East Nimar); false match.
Figure captions and Chandel temple (East Nimar); false match.
Harsud excavation (East Nimar); false match.
Harsud and Saraswati Kunda (East Nimar) pottery; false match.
Pottery comparison with Ahichchhatra types at another site; no location.

author: B. S. Raman (ASI) and Y. Aboshi (Kansai University, Osaka)
evidence: 1987-88: Kushana terraced tank W of the Gandhakuti shrine; circular stupa with monastic cells in four phases (Kushana to early medieval); Kushana monastery; Gupta temple; terracotta Buddha head; two Gupta sealings read Damesgutakaya; occupation 1st to 11th-12th c. AD
quote: resumed excavation at Jetavan (Sravasti) … In area 'A' and 'B' on northwestern fringe of the mound, west of the Gandhakuti shrine, the corner wall noticed earlier was further exposed to discern a tank of Kushana period … The site was in continuous occupation from Kushana to early medieval periods
note: Jetavana = the Sahet mound taken for granted (Cunningham's identification, asr; confirmed by the Jetavana inscription in ar). Mizutani gives no modern site for 06.01.04 (status unknown); this report assumes Sahet. No new inscription naming the vihara.
Epigraphy introduction (Amaravati Museum as a source of inscriptions).
Salankayana inscription originally from Kausambi, now in Allahabad Museum; no location argument.
Loose sculptures at Ellichpur fort, Amaravati district (Maharashtra); false match.
Archaeological Museum, Amaravati: acquisitions.

Conservation (Ghoshitarama fencing, Kausambi; Sahet, Sravasti; Piprahwa stupa).

author: Ajit Kumar Prasad, Directorate of Archaeology, Government of Bihar
asr_identification: mound N of the Mahabodhi temple, Bodh Gaya (Gaya)
evidence: 1988-89: four periods (NBP; Kushana brick structure; Gupta and late Gupta rampart and brick structures with seals, votive stupas; Pala brick-paved floor with seals and sealings, votive stupas)
quote: resumed excavation at Taradih, with a view to ascertain the cultural sequence of the mound located to the north of the Mahabodhi temple at Bodh Gaya … Period IV was represented by antiquities and remains of the Pala period (Period VIII of Taradih). Remains of brick-paved floor were exposed
note: Fixes the position of Taradih: N of the Mahabodhi temple = Mizutani's 'great monastery' mound (08.06.30, Mahabodhi sangharama outside the N gate). No inscription naming the monastery; the report does not cite Xuanzang. Gupta rampart noted.

author: B. M. Pande, Institute of Archaeology, Archaeological Survey of India
evidence: 1988-89: sequence Kushana to late Mughal confirmed; Kushana mud rampart in the rain-gully; successive defence walls up to Mughal times; relation to the Bahari mound sought
quote: The main objective of this season's work was (a) to know more about the lay-out of the house-complexes and material remains of the period, (b) to expose further the partially-exposed palatial-complex … the excavation of rain-gully also revealed the presence of a considerably wide and high mud rampart belonging, in all likelihood, to the Kushana times
note: Beginning of the 1988-89 report; Vardhana-period finds in 494. Thanesar = Sthanesvara assumed, as Mizutani 04.08. Bahari mound = Cunningham's Bahari (asr).

author: B. M. Pande, Institute of Archaeology, Archaeological Survey of India
evidence: 1988-89: Vardhana period (mid-6th to end-7th c.) red ware; fragmentary human head recalling the figure on Harsha's coins; three gold-alloy coins with Brahmi legend; building-complex with 99-course wall traced further; Vardhana fortification wall in TSR-2
quote: The next period of occupation at Thanesar has been identified as the Vardhana period (middle of the sixth century to the end of the seventh century) … The important finds from this period comprise a fragmentary human head, vaguely recalling the figure depicted on the coins of Harsha
note: Occupation and fortification of Thanesar in Harsha's time, i.e. Xuanzang's Sthanesvara; consistent with Mizutani 04.08 and asr. No Buddhist remains.
Excavation elsewhere (Siva-linga feature compared with Amaravati area).
Adam excavation (Nagpur); false match.

author: Dilbar Bhengra (Excavation Branch III, ASI) and Yoshinori Aboshi (Kansai University)
evidence: 1988-89: stupa over a Kushana cell; terraced tank exposed on E and S sides; Gupta temples and votive stupas in Area G; late-Kushana cells; terracotta Buddha figures; four periods Kushana to Gahadavala
quote: resumed the excavation at the Jetavana area, Sravasti, with the objective of exposing the tank and correlating it with the other nearby structures … Period I Kushana/late Kushana (circa first to third century AD) Period II Gupta (circa fourth to seventh century AD)
note: Continues 479; Sahet = Jetavana assumed (asr, ar). Mizutani 06.01.04 has no modern site. Nothing bearing on Xuanzang's description beyond occupation through the 7th c.
Pottery comparison with Ahichchhatra and Hastinapura.
Epigraphy sources list (Amaravati Museum).
Stone inscription from Mangher-Chhatikara (Mathura), Yavana era; no Xiyu ji location.
Persian inscriptions at Sahar (Mathura).
Upper Palaeolithic tools near Dongeshwari cave, Bodhgaya; Brahmanical sculptures at Vadnagar; no location argument (Vadnagar = 11.09 Anandapura not discussed).

author: L. C. Singh, Excavation Branch III, Archaeological Survey of India
asr_identification: stupa and Asokan pillar complex at Kolhua (Vaishali)
evidence: 1989-90: Gupta svastika-shaped and 26 other votive stupas W of the pillar-stupa complex; Kushana-Gupta-post-Gupta monastery (12 cells, entrance facing the main stupa) 80 m SW of the pillar; terracotta plaques with the ye dhamma creed; sherd inscribed Buddha Nandasya karakah parigraha (Gupta Brahmi); NBP to post-Gupta
quote: carried out a limited excavation at the Stupa and Asokan pillar-complex at Kolhua … A monastic establishment (pl. V A) having three structural phases was exposed in Area B corresponding to the Kushana, Gupta and post-Gupta Periods
note: Kolhua pillar and stupa = Mizutani 07.03.04 (Asoka stupa and pillar, Bakhra/Kolhua; asr: Cunningham, Bakhra). Buddhist monastic complex confirmed by excavation; the report does not cite Xuanzang.

author: B. M. Pande, Institute of Archaeology, Archaeological Survey of India
evidence: 1989-90: PGW deposit below Kushana; Kushana mud rampart (two phases); Gupta structural complex and seal reading Vanagrama; Vardhana massive building complex and renovated fortification; a few terracotta plaques perhaps of Buddha (Kushana)
quote: The new features of the preceding period were found to continue in the Vardhana period as well which followed without any break. The most important structure of this period is a massive building complex. During this period the fortification wall was also renovated.
note: Third season; confirms a fortified town in the Vardhana period at Thanesar (Mizutani 04.08). No identification argued; no Buddhist monument found.
Lalitagiri (Cuttack) monastery excavation; Nalanda cited only as a parallel. The report does not link Lalitagiri to Xuanzang (Mizutani 10.09.02 Puspagiri = Khandagiri).

author: K. K. Rishi and Kuldip Singh, Department of Cultural Affairs, Archaeology and Museums, Punjab, under C. Margabandhu (ASI)
evidence: 1989-90: Kushana stupa S-2 of dharma-chakra pattern and stupa S-3 near the SGL-11 monastery (27 cells, 39 x 36 m); coins of Kunindas, Kushanas, Hunas; Kharoshthi-inscribed bowl
quote: This discovery corroborated the description given by Hiuen-Tsang, who travelled India during the time of Harsha Vardhana (AD 606-647); the Chinese pilgrim in his account mentions that there were 10 stupas and monasteries at She-tu-to-lu (now Sanghol).
note: Identifies Satadru's capital (She-tu-to-lu) with Sanghol; Mizutani (04.05, uncertain) gives Sarhind (Cunningham), c. 15 km S of Sanghol. The Xiyu ji has 10 sangharamas, not stupas. No inscription supports the identification; Kushana stupas only.
Exploration at Tulabhita (Malda); false match for Bhita.
Ikshvaku and Satavahana coins from debris clearance around the Amaravati Maha-stupa; no location argument.
Museum notes (Mathura, Sarnath).
Conservation at Sirpur (sculpture shed).
Chemical conservation at Sarnath (Kot stupa, Mulagandhakuti).

Plate list (Kolhua, Harsh-ka-Tila; see 510-511).
Museum plate list (Mathura).
Director-General's preface listing excavations (Kolhua, Sravasti, Sarnath).

author: L. C. Singh, Excavation Branch III, Archaeological Survey of India
asr_identification: Kolhua (Muzaffarpur): Kushana brick-lined tank by the pillar-stupa complex
evidence: 1992-93: Kushana brick-lined tank fully exposed, c. 32.5 x 31.5 m, seven tiers, 4.30 m deep so far, two bathing ghats, corbelled arch, drain
quote: The Kushana brick-lined tank noticed in last year's excavation was fully exposed measuring approximately 32-5 meters east-west and 31-5 meters north-south
note: The tank by the Asoka pillar answers Xuanzang's monkey tank (dug by monkeys for the Buddha) S of the Asoka stupa and pillar (07.03.04), which Cunningham (asr) located at Bakhra/Kolhua; the report does not make the link.

author: L. C. Singh, Excavation Branch III, ASI, with the Japanese team under Y. Aboshi
evidence: 1992-93: square raised platform facing the Suraj Kund tank (stupa or image platform); monastery complex to the S; late cistern and rooms; four periods from pre-NBP to early medieval
quote: The excavation revealed an almost square raised platform with 15 cm projected plan towards east … either to form a square stupa or a platform to install an idol facing Suraj Kund … Towards south was noticed a monastery complex.
note: Work in the city (Maheth) of Sravasti; Sahet-Mahet = Sravasti assumed (Mizutani 06.01; asr; ar). Pre-NBP antiquity of the city; no bearing on Xuanzang's individual sites.

author: A. K. Sinha, Headquarters, Archaeological Survey of India
evidence: 1992-93: trial trenches behind the apsidal structure and between it and the Asokan pillar: apsidal temple built in the late Mauryan period; earliest deposits c. 3rd-4th c. BC (plain grey, black-slipped ware, a few NBP sherds)
quote: carried out trial excavation at Sarnath with an objective to know its antiquity … indicated that the antiquity of the site may not go beyond circa third-fourth century BC. The recent work could also confirm that the apsidal structure was built sometimes in late-Mauryan period
note: Sarnath = Mrgadava assumed (Mizutani 07.01.02a; asr). Dating only; the apsidal temple near the Asoka pillar is not one of Xuanzang's named monuments.
Brahmi memorial-pillar inscription (2nd c. AD) from Dharanikota, in Amaravati Museum; no location argument.
Persian epitaphs at Kosam Inam (18th c.); no bearing.
Conservation of the Laxman temple, Sirpur.

author: D. S. Malik and M. Acharya, Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Haryana
evidence: 1995-96: limited excavation and rain-gully section: Period I NBPW-associated (c. 5th-1st c. BC) with ring-wells; Period II Sunga-Kushan houses of mud and burnt brick, terracottas (c. 1st c. BC-3rd c. AD)
quote: Excavation at Sugh (Amadalpur) (30-9' N; 77-23' E), was conducted under the direction of D.S. Malik and M. Acharya … From the frequent occurrence of ancient name Shugha in various ancient texts it may be presumed that the site was an important place throughout the ancient times.
note: Sugh = Srughna implied by the ancient name; agrees with Mizutani 04.09 and asr (Cunningham). No remains of Xuanzang's period reported (nothing after the 3rd c. AD).

author: K. P. Poonacha, Bangalore Circle, Archaeological Survey of India
evidence: 1995-96: Satavahana-level terracottas incl. Hariti, a Buddha face and a Bodhisattva with a chaitya in the crown, the first stratified Buddhist finds at Banavasi; soapstone casket sherd with pre-Christian Brahmi (Magadha?)
quote: establishing for the first time the Buddhist antiquity of Banavasi in a stratigraphic context. It is to be noted that Hiuen Tsang had visited Banavasi (ancient Vaijayanti) and had noticed many stupas towards the north of the township.
note: Treats Banavasi as a city visited by Xuanzang (as IAR 1970-71, Mysore University); differs from Mizutani 11.02 (Konkanapura, capital Annagundi on the Tungabhadra, disputed). The Buddhist finds are Satavahana-period, not 7th-c.

author: L. C. Singh, Excavation Branch III, ASI, with Y. Aboshi, Archaeological Research Institute, Kansai University
asr_identification: Maheth, Sravasti (Bahraich): Khairatal and Surajkund area
evidence: 1995-96: Area C (200 m S of Surajkund, E of Khairatal): fortification eroded; three structural phases; two house-complexes with Kushan-size bricks in the foundation and Gupta superstructure
quote: resumed digging with a view to ascertaining the habitational pattern besides the antiquity of the site near Khairatal area … The bricks which were used in the foundation of these structures were of Kushan bricks size. The structures above the foundation however, appeared to be of the Gupta period.
note: Domestic quarter of the city of Sravasti (Maheth); identification assumed, as Mizutani 06.01. No Buddhist monument.

author: L. C. Singh, Excavation Branch III, ASI, with Y. Aboshi, Archaeological Research Institute, Kansai University
asr_identification: Maheth, Sravasti (Bahraich): Area C near Surajkund
evidence: 1995-96: house-complexes 1-2 in Area C, Kushan foundations and Gupta superstructure, courtyards, hauz and drain
quote: The earliest phase of construction resembled the Kushan style while the latest phase that of the Gupta period, laid directly on the structural remains of Kushan period.
note: Continuation of 544 (same report). Sravasti = Maheth assumed (Mizutani 06.01).
Pottery comparison (Ahichchhatra XA type) at another site.

author: B. R. Mani, Excavation Branch-II, Archaeological Survey of India
asr_identification: Sankisa (Farrukhabad) = Sankasya, the place of the descent from the Trayastrimsa heaven
evidence: 1995-96: first stratified excavation; mounds over c. 6 km periphery within an earthen rampart; brick stupa mound 300 m S of the village under the Bisharidevi temple; Asokan elephant capital; PGW to Kushan sequence
quote: identified with Sankasya. It is referred to as the royal city and the capital of Kusadhvaja … with Sankassa mentioned in Pali Buddhist texts as the place where Buddha accompanied with Brahma and Indra descended from the trayastrimsa heaven … Nearly 300 m due south is another mound of solid brick-work, supposed to be a stupa, topped by a late medieval temple of Bisharidevi
note: Sankisa = Kapitha capital and the Devavatara site assumed (Cunningham, asr); Mizutani 04.15/04.15.02 call it disputed. Excavation gives PGW-Kushan sequence; nothing of Xuanzang's period or of the ladders' monastery.
Tulabhita (Jagajjibanpur, Malda) Pala monastery; false match for Bhita.
Prakrit memorial-pillar inscription from Dharanikota in Amaravati Museum; no location argument.
